dataFlow: When a shopper visits a sold-out product page the widget calls GET /widget/availability to determine whether to render (suppressed on in-stock items) and GET /widget/signup to surface any existing signup for that email+item. The shopper submits their email via POST /widget/signup, which is deduplicated and stored as an active waitlist entry with a queue position. When inventory rises above zero (inventory_levels/update webhook fires), the backend resolves the affected variant via the inventoryItem admin query, identifies all active waitlist entries for that variant ordered by queue position, and opens a restock event — it then fans out notification emails up to the available quantity and marks each notified entry as notified, leaving the rest active for the next restock. When an order is paid (orders/paid webhook), the backend checks whether any notified waitlist entry for that customer email and any purchased variant falls within the 7-day conversion window and records it as converted. When a product is deleted (products/delete webhook), all waitlist entries for that product are immediately purged. The merchant uses the admin dashboard to see a queue-size ranking, drill into per-product subscriber lists, export CSV, edit the notification template, and configure quiet hours.

triggers.event: inventory level for a variant rises above zero
triggers.idempotency: if a restock event already exists for the same inventory item external id in an open or dispatching state, treat the delivery as a no-op

payloadBindings.resolution: resolve from inventory_item_id via the inventoryItem admin GraphQL query returning inventoryItem.variant.id

triggers.event: a product is deleted from the store
triggers.idempotency: purging entries for an already-purged product is a no-op

triggers.event: a customer completes a paid order
triggers.idempotency: if a conversion record already exists for this order external id, treat the event as a no-op

capabilities.description: Query Shopify for the current availability of a product or variant so the widget knows whether to render the signup form.
Record a shopper's email on the waitlist for a sold-out item, assigning a queue position and deduplicating same-email same-item requests.
Mark all active waitlist entries for the email behind a given unsubscribe token as unsubscribed.
Resolve a variant external id from an inventory item external id via a Shopify admin lookup.

shopifySteps.produces: variant external id and product external id

capabilities.description: Create a restock event record for an item whose inventory has risen above zero, computing the notification budget from available quantity and active waitlist count.
Send notification emails to waitlist entries at the front of the queue up to the restock event's notification budget, respecting quiet hours, and mark each notified entry as notified.
Delete or mark purged all waitlist entries for a product when that product is deleted from the store.
Match a paid order's line items against recently notified waitlist entries within the 7-day attribution window and record each conversion.
Return a paginated, filterable list of waitlist entries for a given product or variant for the admin drill-in view.
Stream all subscriber entries for a given product or variant as a CSV file.
Return products ranked by active waitlist size for the merchant admin overview.
Return aggregate counts of total signups, notifications sent, and conversions for the merchant dashboard.
Persist the merchant's notification template content and quiet-hours window.

persistence.name: waitlist_entries
persistence.purpose: Stores every shopper signup for a sold-out item, tracks queue position, notification status, and conversion.

columns.name: item_external_id
columns.purpose: the variant or product external id the shopper is waiting on; combined with item_scope to determine the level of the signup

columns.name: item_scope
columns.purpose: discriminates between a variant-level and a product-level signup (values: variant, product)

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: always the parent product external id; used to purge all entries on product deletion without a join

columns.name: queue_position
columns.purpose: monotonically increasing integer within each item, used to fan out notifications in sign-up order

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: lifecycle: active, notified, converted, unsubscribed, purged

columns.name: unsubscribe_token
columns.purpose: opaque token embedded in every notification email for one-click global unsubscribe

columns.name: restock_event_id
columns.purpose: set when the entry is notified; references the restock_events row that triggered the notification, enforcing one notification per restock per entry

queryPatterns: active entries for a given item_external_id ordered by queue_position ascending (notification fan-out)
all entries for a given product_external_id (bulk purge on deletion)
single entry by email and item_external_id (dedup check on signup)
all active entries for a given email (global unsubscribe)
entries for a given item_external_id filtered by status with cursor pagination (admin drill-in)
entries with status=notified and email matching a paid-order contact email within 7 days of notified_at (conversion matching)

persistence.name: restock_events
persistence.purpose: Records each distinct restock event for an item so the system knows which entries have already been notified for a given restock and prevents duplicate blasts.

columns.name: item_external_id
columns.purpose: the variant or product external id that was restocked

columns.name: item_scope
columns.purpose: discriminates variant-level vs product-level, mirrors waitlist_entries.item_scope

columns.name: inventory_item_external_id
columns.purpose: the inventory item id from the webhook, used as the idempotency key to prevent duplicate restock events

columns.name: available_quantity
columns.purpose: units available at the moment the restock was detected; governs how many waitlist positions to notify

columns.name: notification_budget
columns.purpose: number of entries authorised to be notified in this event; computed as min(available_quantity, active_waitlist_count)

columns.name: notified_count
columns.purpose: running count of entries actually notified in this event; incremented as emails are dispatched

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: event lifecycle: open, dispatching, completed

queryPatterns: latest open or dispatching event for a given item_external_id (idempotency check on new inventory_levels/update delivery)
single event by id (update notified_count and status as emails are dispatched)

persistence.name: conversion_records
persistence.purpose: Records confirmed conversions where a notified shopper purchased the item within the 7-day attribution window.

columns.name: waitlist_entry_id
columns.purpose: the waitlist entry credited with the conversion

columns.name: order_external_id
columns.purpose: the paid order that triggered the conversion check; also the idempotency key for duplicate orders/paid deliveries

columns.name: item_external_id
columns.purpose: the specific item that was purchased, for per-item conversion stats

queryPatterns: count by item_external_id (admin stats per product/variant)
lookup by order_external_id (idempotency on duplicate orders/paid delivery)

persistence.name: notification_settings
persistence.purpose: Merchant-configured notification template content and quiet-hours window; singleton row.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: singleton row guard; application code enforces at most one row

columns.name: template_subject
columns.purpose: merchant-authored subject line supporting {{product_name}} and {{item_details}} tokens

columns.name: template_body
columns.purpose: merchant-authored message body supporting {{product_name}}, {{item_details}}, and {{unsubscribe_url}} tokens

columns.name: quiet_hours_start
columns.purpose: hour-of-day (0-23) at which the quiet window begins; no notifications sent during the quiet window

columns.name: quiet_hours_end
columns.purpose: hour-of-day (0-23) at which the quiet window ends

queryPatterns: single row read before every notification dispatch to check quiet hours and render template

externalContracts.purpose: Return whether a given product or variant is currently sold out so the widget knows whether to render the signup form.
Check whether a given email is already on the waitlist for an item so the widget can render the correct initial state.
Register a shopper's email on the waitlist for a sold-out product or variant.
Remove a shopper from all active waitlists via the one-click unsubscribe link in notification emails.
Return products ranked by active waitlist size for the main admin overview.
Return the paginated list of individual subscriber entries for a given product or variant.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update deliveries for the same inventory item with available > 0 — check for an open or dispatching restock event for that inventory item before creating a new one; second delivery is a no-op.

Stock rises, notifications go out, stock immediately sells through and rises again before all entries are notified — the second rise creates a new restock event with a fresh notification budget; entries already notified in the first event are not re-notified unless they return to active status.
Quiet hours are active when notifications are ready to dispatch — hold the entire batch until the quiet window ends; do not send a partial batch that straddles the boundary.
Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order external id — the conversion_records unique key on (waitlist_entry_id, order_external_id) makes the upsert idempotent; no double-credit.

Notification email delivery fails for one entry in a batch — log the failure and continue dispatching remaining entries; do not roll back the restock event; the failed entry retains its notified status so the merchant can diagnose via the admin drill-in.

Same email signs up for the same item a second time after a previous unsubscribe — the unique key on (email, item_external_id) blocks a duplicate insert; return already_existed flag to the widget without error.
products/delete fires for a product with no active waitlist entries — purge is a no-op; do not error.
Paid order has no email address in the contact_email field — skip conversion matching for that order and log the gap; do not crash the handler.
